content:
maya: quick sync on a weird state I found in the capacity editor. when you edit min/max for Pool A, then switch pools, the inputs show the edited numbers but look disabled. users might think those values are live for the new pool. :confused:

alex: can you paste the steps? I remember a 'sticky draft' prototype but not sure if we landed on final behavior.

maya: steps: open Pool A, change Min 2 -> 4 and Max 6 -> 8, then pick Pool B from the pool picker. UI greys the fields and shows 4 / 8 with a faint dashed outline. no hint those are drafts for Pool A.

liam: risky. my suggestion: add a visible "Draft for Pool A" pill above the inputs that stays keyboard-focusable. clicking it shows actions: Apply to Pool B, Discard draft, Edit. pill should show validation state (check/warning).

rachel: copy recs: full copy "Draft changes saved for Pool A". condensed for mobile: "Draft · Pool A". action buttons: "Apply changes" (primary) and "Discard" (link).

zoe: accessibility: when the pill appears announce via aria-live polite: "Draft changes saved for Pool A" and focus should move to the pill so keyboard users immediately know something changed. provide keyboard handlers: Enter to open pill actions, Escape to discard.

alex: do drafts persist across navigation or are they ephemeral?

maya: proposing session-scoped persistence (localStorage) with a 24h TTL. show a non-modal toast after navigation: "You have unsaved capacity changes for Pool A  Continue editing  Discard". include cost estimate inline if possible.

liam: backend note: some pools have max_below_limit constraints; if the drafted Min exceeds target pool capacity we should show an inline validation under the pill: "Min (4) exceeds Pool B max (2)." with actions: "Choose compatible pool" or "Adjust Min". Prevent Apply until resolved.

rachel: wording for that error: "Selected Min (4) exceeds Pool B maximum (2). Reduce Min or pick a different pool." more actionable than generic messages.

zoe: for screen readers use role/status for the pill announcements. For blocking errors on Apply use assertive. Ensure all action buttons have accessible names and visible focus outlines.

alex: SLO slider behavior question: currently switching pools reverts SLO to pool default which surprised Simone. Should SLO be route-scoped?

maya: SLO should be route-level preference and persist across pool switches. Only if the selected pool cannot meet the SLO show a clear warning and suggested actions. Example: "This pool cannot meet the requested latency SLO. Switch to a higher-priority pool or relax SLO."

liam: backend can expose a capability flag per pool. if flag false, render SLO slider disabled with tooltip "This pool cannot deliver the selected SLO" and offer "Find compatible pools" which opens a filtered pool picker.

rachel: microcopy for the filter: primary "Show pools that meet current SLO" and secondary "Show all pools". keep the filter sticky while the user navigates.

maya: burst copy: change ambiguous "Allow burst" to "Allow temporary burst (up to X GPUs)" and add an info icon linking to docs. if draft enables burst but target pool has no burst capacity show dashed warning: "Burst unavailable for Pool B".

zoe: focus order: burst toggle -> info icon -> burst amount slider. info icon needs aria-label and must be reachable by keyboard. Also ensure the turbo/burst slider announces values while dragging.

rachel: for the toast we should include a token-level cost CTA: "Apply changes — estimated cost +$0.13/hr" so users can see immediate cost impact. include it in the Apply button label if space allows.

deploy-bot: preview build: capacity-drafts/ghost-state-v2  https://staging.redwood/preview/1746010000 (expires in 3h) :rocket:

alex: thanks folks. maya can you mock the pill + toast + updated copy and prepare a 15-min review tomorrow 11:00? :calendar:

maya: will upload prototype in 30m.

liam: when you do, include a short keyboard testing script and the validation matrix for pool capabilities. I'll run integration tests once the PR is ready.

zoe: include a small accessibility checklist in the PR: live region behavior, focus order, aria-labels, keyboard acceptance criteria, and screen reader readme snippet.

rachel: tiny design nit: use a 12px capsule for the pill in tight layouts and 14px on desktop. color tokens: bg info-50, border info-200. add a subtle success (green) and warning (amber) icon states.

maya: noted. thanks everyone! :raised_hands:
